blocks.text:
Conventions match (var, plain functions). The code follows existing patterns well.

Let me wait for the coverage job and then run the ratchet. Meanwhile check a few more review angles:

1. `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` vs `_prListHeadRepo` — duplication! The two functions are near-identical (the smProvider one also accepts `nameWithOwner`). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT/SUGESTION). They can't easily share code since they're in different layers (smProvider is common layer, githubSource is sm layer — actually githubSource could require smProvider? smProvider is in js/common/, githubSource in js/sm/sources/. Requires must be hoisted. githubSource probably already requires something from common. Let me check.)

2. The security angle: headFull is derived from PR payload (attacker-controlled — anyone can open a fork PR). `parts[0]`/`parts[1]` are used as workspace/repository in github_list_branches MCP call. Could a malicious fork name inject something? Repo names on GitHub are restricted ([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]), owner names too. So no injection realistically. The parts.length===2 check means "a/b/c" stays base. OK.

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

4. What about a fork PR where headFull === base full name from a DIFFERENT casing? Not realistic.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. It's consistent with dead-head semantics (can't verify head → treat as gone), but the PR description claims "A deleted fork (head.repo: null) resolves to headRepo: null → base probe → fail-open" — that's for deleted forks which keep item. For live-but-unreadable forks: benched. Fine, note as SUGESTION.

6. Duplication between the two resolvers — real finding. Given CRAP failure is the blocking issue, the natural fix for CRAP is to extract/simplify and add tests covering all branches (string spec, nameWithOwner, owner-only). Both flagged functions exceed threshold partly due to uncovered branches: `typeof r === 'string'` and `nameWithOwner` paths have no tests. Adding tests for those branches raises coverage and drops CRAP below 8. And merging the two duplicates into one shared helper would halve the complexity.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T18:39:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

# gh-1057: Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)

## Description

## Problem

The gh-922 dead-head park never lifts for **fork (cross-repository) PRs**, even after the source branch is restored: the park oracle probes the head branch in the BASE repo, where a fork's branch can never exist.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, flutter_agent_harness PR #1591)

- Fork PR from `YuryBY:fix/android-dap-home-sandbox`; the branch was deleted → correctly parked dead-head.
- The branch was **restored** (fork head `ca925a0e`, `refs/pull/1591/head` live).
- The 18:06Z tick still benched it: `🪦 benched dead-head park pr-1591 — head ref fix/android-dap-home-sandbox is gone (gh-922)` — twice in one tick.
- The branch is 404 only in the base repo (`IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`); in the fork it exists.

## Root cause

`smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` → `_ghBranchExists(owner, repo, name)` always probes the deployment's base `owner/repo`. `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` calls it with just the branch name — the PR item's `head.repo` (fork owner) is never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the probe is a guaranteed 404 → permanent park.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dead-head probe resolves the PR's **head repository** (`pullRequest.head.repo.full_name` / owner) and checks the branch THERE; same-repo PRs keep today's behavior.
- [ ] A restored fork branch un-benches the PR on the next tick (park label removed or the item simply re-enters the queue per existing park-reset lanes).
- [ ] Unit tests: cross-repo PR with branch missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; branch missing in BOTH stays benched; fail-open on probe errors preserved.
- [ ] No change for same-repo PRs (regression test).

## Non-goals

- Rework-on-fork push permissions (a machine cannot push to a guest fork — separate policy question, out of scope here).

## Machine jobs

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

- name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*…

blocks.text:
- name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Conventions match (var, plain functions). The code follows existing patterns well.

Let me wait for the coverage job and then run the ratchet. Meanwhile check a few more review angles:

1. `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` vs `_prListHeadRepo` — duplication! The two functions are near-identical (the smProvider one also accepts `nameWithOwner`). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT/SUGESTION). They can't easily share code since they're in different layers (smProvider is common layer, githubSource is sm layer — actually githubSource could require smProvider? smProvider is in js/common/, githubSource in js/sm/sources/. Requires must be hoisted. githubSource probably already requires something from common. Let me check.)

2. The security angle: headFull is derived from PR payload (attacker-controlled — anyone can open a fork PR). `parts[0]`/`parts[1]` are used as workspace/repository in github_list_branches MCP call. Could a malicious fork name inject something? Repo names on GitHub are restricted ([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]), owner names too. So no injection realistically. The parts.length===2 check means "a/b/c" stays base. OK.

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

4. What about a fork PR where headFull === base full name from a DIFFERENT casing? Not realistic.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. It's consistent with dead-head semantics (can't verify head → treat as gone), but the PR description claims "A deleted fork (head.repo: null) resolves to headRepo: null → base probe → fail-open" — that's for deleted forks which keep item. For live-but-unreadable forks: benched. Fine, note as SUGESTION.

6. Duplication between the two resolvers — real finding. Given CRAP failure is the blocking issue, the natural fix for CRAP is to extract/simplify and add tests covering all branches (string spec, nameWithOwner, owner-only). Both flagged functions exceed threshold partly due to uncovered branches: `typeof r === 'string'` and `nameWithOwner` paths have no tests. Adding tests for those branches raises coverage and drops CRAP below 8. And merging the two duplicates into one shared helper would halve the complexity.

- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +211

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T18:39:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

# gh-1057: Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)

## Description

## Problem

The gh-922 dead-head park never lifts for **fork (cross-repository) PRs**, even after the source branch is restored: the park oracle probes the head branch in the BASE repo, where a fork's branch can never exist.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, flutter_agent_harness PR #1591)

- Fork PR from `YuryBY:fix/android-dap-home-sandbox`; the branch was deleted → correctly parked dead-head.
- The branch was **restored** (fork head `ca925a0e`, `refs/pull/1591/head` live).
- The 18:06Z tick still benched it: `🪦 benched dead-head park pr-1591 — head ref fix/android-dap-home-sandbox is gone (gh-922)` — twice in one tick.
- The branch is 404 only in the base repo (`IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`); in the fork it exists.

## Root cause

`smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` → `_ghBranchExists(owner, repo, name)` always probes the deployment's base `owner/repo`. `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` calls it with just the branch name — the PR item's `head.repo` (fork owner) is never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the probe is a guaranteed 404 → permanent park.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dead-head probe resolves the PR's **head repository** (`pullRequest.head.repo.full_name` / owner) and checks the branch THERE; same-repo PRs keep today's behavior.
- [ ] A restored fork branch un-benches the PR on the next tick (park label removed or the item simply re-enters the queue per existing park-reset lanes).
- [ ] Unit tests: cross-repo PR with branch missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; branch missing in BOTH stays benched; fail-open on probe errors preserved.
- [ ] No change for same-repo PRs (regression test).

## Non-goals

- Rework-on-fork push permissions (a machine cannot push to a guest fork — separate policy question, out of scope here).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'

blocks.text:
- name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

They can't easily share code since they're in different layers (smProvider is common layer, githubSource is sm layer — actually githubSource could require smProvider? smProvider is in js/common/, githubSource in js/sm/sources/. 2. The security angle: headFull is derived from PR payload (attacker-controlled — anyone can open a fork PR). `parts[0]`/`parts[1]` are used as workspace/repository in github_list_branches MCP call. Could a malicious fork name inject something? Repo names on GitHub are restricted ([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]), owner names too. So no injection realistically. The parts.length===2 check means "a/b/c" stays base. OK.

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

4. What about a fork PR where headFull === base full name from a DIFFERENT casing? Not realistic.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. It's consistent with dead-head semantics (can't verify head → treat as gone), but the PR description claims "A deleted fork (head.repo: null) resolves to headRepo: null → base probe → fail-open" — that's for deleted forks which keep item. For live-but-unreadable forks: benched. Fine, note as SUGESTION.

6. Duplication between the two resolvers — real finding. Given CRAP failure is the blocking issue, the natural fix for CRAP is to extract/simplify and add tests covering all branches (string spec, nameWithOwner, owner-only). Both flagged functions exceed threshold partly due to uncovered branches: `typeof r === 'string'` and `nameWithOwner` paths have no tests. Adding tests for those branches raises coverage and drops CRAP below 8. And merging the two duplicates into one shared helper would halve the complexity.

- **PR #**: 1059

- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T18:39:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

# gh-1057: Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)

## Description

## Problem

The gh-922 dead-head park never lifts for **fork (cross-repository) PRs**, even after the source branch is restored: the park oracle probes the head branch in the BASE repo, where a fork's branch can never exist.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, flutter_agent_harness PR #1591)

- Fork PR from `YuryBY:fix/android-dap-home-sandbox`; the branch was deleted → correctly parked dead-head.
- The branch was **restored** (fork head `ca925a0e`, `refs/pull/1591/head` live).
- The 18:06Z tick still benched it: `🪦 benched dead-head park pr-1591 — head ref fix/android-dap-home-sandbox is gone (gh-922)` — twice in one tick.
- The branch is 404 only in the base repo (`IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`); in the fork it exists.

## Root cause

`smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` → `_ghBranchExists(owner, repo, name)` always probes the deployment's base `owner/repo`. `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` calls it with just the branch name — the PR item's `head.repo` (fork owner) is never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the probe is a guaranteed 404 → permanent park.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dead-head probe resolves the PR's **head repository** (`pullRequest.head.repo.full_name` / owner) and checks the branch THERE; same-repo PRs keep today's behavior.
- [ ] A restored fork branch un-benches the PR on the next tick (park label removed or the item simply re-enters the queue per existing park-reset lanes).
- [ ] Unit tests: cross-repo PR with branch missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; branch missing in BOTH stays benched; fail-open on probe errors preserved.
- [ ] No change for same-repo PRs (regression test).

## Non-goals

- Rework-on-fork push permissions (a machine cannot push to a guest fork — separate policy question, out of scope here).

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

blocks.text:
- name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

blocks.text:
Conventions match (var, plain functions). The code follows existing patterns well.

Let me wait for the coverage job and then run the ratchet. Meanwhile check a few more review angles:

1. `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` vs `_prListHeadRepo` — duplication! The two functions are near-identical (the smProvider one also accepts `nameWithOwner`). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT/SUGESTION). They can't easily share code since they're in different layers (smProvider is common layer, githubSource is sm layer — actually githubSource could require smProvider? smProvider is in js/common/, githubSource in js/sm/sources/. Requires must be hoisted. githubSource probably already requires something from common. Let me check.)

2. The security angle: headFull is derived from PR payload (attacker-controlled — anyone can open a fork PR). `parts[0]`/`parts[1]` are used as workspace/repository in github_list_branches MCP call. Could a malicious fork name inject something? Repo names on GitHub are restricted ([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]), owner names too. So no injection realistically. The parts.length===2 check means "a/b/c" stays base. OK.

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

4. What about a fork PR where headFull === base full name from a DIFFERENT casing? Not realistic.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +211
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T18:39:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

# gh-1057: Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)

## Description

## Problem

The gh-922 dead-head park never lifts for **fork (cross-repository) PRs**, even after the source branch is restored: the park oracle probes the head branch in the BASE repo, where a fork's branch can never exist.

## Live evidence (2026-10-18, flutter_agent_harness PR #1591)

- Fork PR from `YuryBY:fix/android-dap-home-sandbox`; the branch was deleted → correctly parked dead-head.
- The branch was **restored** (fork head `ca925a0e`, `refs/pull/1591/head` live).
- The 18:06Z tick still benched it: `🪦 benched dead-head park pr-1591 — head ref fix/android-dap-home-sandbox is gone (gh-922)` — twice in one tick.
- The branch is 404 only in the base repo (`IstiN/flutter_agent_harness`); in the fork it exists.

## Root cause

`smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` → `_ghBranchExists(owner, repo, name)` always probes the deployment's base `owner/repo`. `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` calls it with just the branch name — the PR item's `head.repo` (fork owner) is never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the probe is a guaranteed 404 → permanent park.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The dead-head probe resolves the PR's **head repository** (`pullRequest.head.repo.full_name` / owner) and checks the branch THERE; same-repo PRs keep today's behavior.
- [ ] A restored fork branch un-benches the PR on the next tick (park label removed or the item simply re-enters the queue per existing park-reset lanes).
- [ ] Unit tests: cross-repo PR with branch missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; branch missing in BOTH stays benched; fail-open on probe errors preserved.
- [ ] No change for same-repo PRs (regression test).

## Non-goals

- Rework-on-fork push permissions (a machine cannot push to a guest fork — separate policy question, out of scope here).
