blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

1. `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` vs `_prListHeadRepo` — duplication! The two functions are near-identical (the smProvider one also accepts `nameWithOwner`). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT/SUGESTION). They can't easily share code since they're in different layers (smProvider is common layer, githubSource is sm layer — actually githubSource could require smProvider? smProvider is in js/common/, githubSource in js/sm/sources/. Requires must be hoisted. githubSource probably already requires something from common. Let me check.)

2. The security angle: headFull is derived from PR payload (attacker-controlled — anyone can open a fork PR). `parts[0]`/`parts[1]` are used as workspace/repository in github_list_branches MCP call. Could a malicious fork name inject something? Repo names on GitHub are restricted ([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]), owner names too. So no injection realistically. The parts.length===2 check means "a/b/c" stays base. OK.

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

4. What about a fork PR where headFull === base full name from a DIFFERENT casing? Not realistic.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. It's consistent with dead-head semantics (can't verify head → treat as gone), but the PR description claims "A deleted fork (head.repo: null) resolves to headRepo: null → base probe → fail-open" — that's for deleted forks which keep item. For live-but-unreadable forks: benched. Fine, note as SUGESTION.

6. Duplication between the two resolvers — real finding. Given CRAP failure is the blocking issue, the natural fix for CRAP is to extract/simplify and add tests covering all branches (string spec, nameWithOwner, owner-only). Both flagged functions exceed threshold partly due to uncovered branches: `typeof r === 'string'` and `nameWithOwner` paths have no tests. Adding tests for those branches raises coverage and drops CRAP below 8. And merging the two duplicates into one shared helper would halve the complexity.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

1. `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` vs `_prListHeadRepo` — duplication! The two functions are near-identical (the smProvider one also accepts `nameWithOwner`). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT/SUGESTION). They can't easily share code since they're in different layers (smProvider is common layer, githubSource is sm layer — actually githubSource could require smProvider? smProvider is in js/common/, githubSource in js/sm/sources/. Requires must be hoisted. githubSource probably already requires something from common. Let me check.)

2. The security angle: headFull is derived from PR payload (attacker-controlled — anyone can open a fork PR). `parts[0]`/`parts[1]` are used as workspace/repository in github_list_branches MCP call. Could a malicious fork name inject something? Repo names on GitHub are restricted ([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]), owner names too. So no injection realistically. The parts.length===2 check means "a/b/c" stays base. OK.

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

4. What about a fork PR where headFull === base full name from a DIFFERENT casing? Not realistic.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. It's consistent with dead-head semantics (can't verify head → treat as gone), but the PR description claims "A deleted fork (head.repo: null) resolves to headRepo: null → base probe → fail-open" — that's for deleted forks which keep item. For live-but-unreadable forks: benched. Fine, note as SUGESTION.

6. Duplication between the two resolvers — real finding. Given CRAP failure is the blocking issue, the natural fix for CRAP is to extract/simplify and add tests covering all branches (string spec, nameWithOwner, owner-only). Both flagged functions exceed threshold partly due to uncovered branches: `typeof r === 'string'` and `nameWithOwner` paths have no tests. Adding tests for those branches raises coverage and drops CRAP below 8. And merging the two duplicates into one shared helper would halve the complexity.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

1. `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` vs `_prListHeadRepo` — duplication! The two functions are near-identical (the smProvider one also accepts `nameWithOwner`). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT/SUGESTION). They can't easily share code since they're in different layers (smProvider is common layer, githubSource is sm layer — actually githubSource could require smProvider? smProvider is in js/common/, githubSource in js/sm/sources/. Requires must be hoisted. githubSource probably already requires something from common. Let me check.)

2. The security angle: headFull is derived from PR payload (attacker-controlled — anyone can open a fork PR). `parts[0]`/`parts[1]` are used as workspace/repository in github_list_branches MCP call. Could a malicious fork name inject something? Repo names on GitHub are restricted ([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]), owner names too. So no injection realistically. The parts.length===2 check means "a/b/c" stays base. OK.

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

4. What about a fork PR where headFull === base full name from a DIFFERENT casing? Not realistic.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. It's consistent with dead-head semantics (can't verify head → treat as gone), but the PR description claims "A deleted fork (head.repo: null) resolves to headRepo: null → base probe → fail-open" — that's for deleted forks which keep item. For live-but-unreadable forks: benched. Fine, note as SUGESTION.

6. Duplication between the two resolvers — real finding. Given CRAP failure is the blocking issue, the natural fix for CRAP is to extract/simplify and add tests covering all branches (string spec, nameWithOwner, owner-only). Both flagged functions exceed threshold partly due to uncovered branches: `typeof r === 'string'` and `nameWithOwner` paths have no tests. Adding tests for those branches raises coverage and drops CRAP below 8. And merging the two duplicates into one shared helper would halve the complexity.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. It's consistent with dead-head semantics (can't verify head → treat as gone), but the PR description claims "A deleted fork (head.repo: null) resolves to headRepo: null → base probe → fail-open" — that's for deleted forks which keep item. For live-but-unreadable forks: benched. Fine, note as SUGESTION.

6. Duplication between the two resolvers — real finding. Given CRAP failure is the blocking issue, the natural fix for CRAP is to extract/simplify and add tests covering all branches (string spec, nameWithOwner, owner-only). Both flagged functions exceed threshold partly due to uncovered branches: `typeof r === 'string'` and `nameWithOwner` paths have no tests. - **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17

- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

blocks.text:
Conventions match (var, plain functions). The code follows existing patterns well.

Let me wait for the coverage job and then run the ratchet. Meanwhile check a few more review angles:

1. `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` vs `_prListHeadRepo` — duplication! The two functions are near-identical (the smProvider one also accepts `nameWithOwner`). That's a duplication finding (IMPORTANT/SUGESTION). They can't easily share code since they're in different layers (smProvider is common layer, githubSource is sm layer — actually githubSource could require smProvider? smProvider is in js/common/, githubSource in js/sm/sources/. Requires must be hoisted. githubSource probably already requires something from common. Let me check.)

2. The security angle: headFull is derived from PR payload (attacker-controlled — anyone can open a fork PR). `parts[0]`/`parts[1]` are used as workspace/repository in github_list_branches MCP call. Could a malicious fork name inject something? Repo names on GitHub are restricted ([a-zA-Z0-9_.-]), owner names too. So no injection realistically. The parts.length===2 check means "a/b/c" stays base. OK.

3. The `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` — pr status may be stale relative to list payload; fine, fail-open.

4. What about a fork PR where headFull === base full name from a DIFFERENT casing? Not realistic.

5. Potential issue: `_ghBranchExistsRef` redirect probes a fork repo via the machine's token — for private forks or repos the token can't access, branchHead throws → branchHead returns null? Look at _ghBranchExists: probe failure "reads as absent" per comment at line ~478: "Empty ref fails closed; probe failure reads as absent." So if the fork is inaccessible to the token (private fork), the probe returns false → the parked fork PR gets benched! Wait, but that was pre-existing behavior for the base repo too. Hmm, but the PR description says fail-open is in isDeadHeadParked (try/catch). But branchExists itself doesn't throw — _ghBranchExists catches probe errors and returns null → false. So "a probe error keeps the item" — in githubSource, provider.branchExists throwing is caught. But smProvider's branchExists never throws; it returns false on probe error → bench verdict → item removed. Is that a behavior change? No — same as before for base repo. But forks: if the machine's GITHUB_TOKEN can't read the fork repo (e.g., fork from an org the token can't access — actually GitHub Actions tokens CAN read fork PR head refs via the base repo's refs/pull/N/head... but branch listing on the fork repo itself requires access; for public forks fine, for private forks of private repos the token may have access). PR notes say "Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope". The #639 single-branch probe uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/{name}` against the fork — for a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN of the base repo may get 404 even though the branch exists via refs/pull/N/head. Hmm — but the branchHeadsMap listing would also 404/empty. That's an edge: fork exists but token can't read it → probe false → parked forever again (same failure mode as the bug being fixed, but narrower). Worth a SUGESTION/IMPORTANT note? The fail-safe claim in the PR ("absent/same-repo/malformed keeps base probe") — but an *unreadable* fork redirects the probe and gets a guaranteed false, which benches the item. Actually wait — would it? The pre-existing behavior benched all forks; the fix helps public forks. For unreadable forks, behavior = bench (same as before the PR). Not a regression, but worth noting that the fail-open story in the description ("throwing probe keeps the item") only covers exceptions, not false-returning probes — the "gone/everywhere" test asserts false → benched. So an unreadable fork = looks gone = benched. It's consistent with dead-head semantics (can't verify head → treat as gone), but the PR description claims "A deleted fork (head.repo: null) resolves to headRepo: null → base probe → fail-open" — that's for deleted forks which keep item. For live-but-unreadable forks: benched. Fine, note as SUGESTION.

6. Duplication between the two resolvers — real finding. Given CRAP failure is the blocking issue, the natural fix for CRAP is to extract/simplify and add tests covering all branches (string spec, nameWithOwner, owner-only). Both flagged functions exceed threshold partly due to uncovered branches: `typeof r === 'string'` and `nameWithOwner` paths have no tests. Adding tests for those branches raises coverage and drops CRAP below 8. And merging the two duplicates into one shared helper would halve the complexity.

### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

```javascript
function _ghRepoOwnerLogin(repo) {
    var o = repo && repo.owner;
    if (!o) return '';
    return o.login || o.name || '';
}

function _ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr) {
    var r = pr && pr.head && pr.head.repo;
    if (!r) return null;
    if (typeof r === 'string') return r.indexOf('/') !== -1 ? r : null;
    if (r.full_name) return r.full_name;
    if (r.nameWithOwner) return r.nameWithOwner;

    return owner && r.name ? owner + '/' + r.name : null;

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

function _ghRepoOwnerLogin(repo) {
    var o = repo && repo.owner;
    if (!o) return '';

function _ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr) {
    var r = pr && pr.head && pr.head.repo;
    if (!r) return null;
    if (typeof r === 'string') return r.indexOf('/') !== -1 ? r : null;

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

```javascript
function _ghRepoOwnerLogin(repo) {
    var o = repo && repo.owner;
    if (!o) return '';
    return o.login || o.name || '';
}

function _ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr) {
    var r = pr && pr.head && pr.head.repo;
    if (!r) return null;
    if (typeof r === 'string') return r.indexOf('/') !== -1 ? r : null;

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

function _ghRepoOwnerLogin(repo) {
    var o = repo && repo.owner;
    if (!o) return '';

function _ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr) {
    var r = pr && pr.head && pr.head.repo;
    if (!r) return null;
    if (typeof r === 'string') return r.indexOf('/') !== -1 ? r : null;

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CRAP ratchet failure — `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` is a new function over threshold (13.8 > 8)**

The `crap` quality gate fails on this PR with:

```text
NEW > 8  js/common/smProvider.js::_ghPrHeadRepoFull: 13.8
NEW > 8  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::_prListHeadRepo: 22.4
0 regression(s), 2 new over threshold ... (exit code 2)
```

Reproduced locally with the pinned tool (`crap4js@83ee6201`) and the released `crap-baseline` asset: cyclomatic complexity **12**, coverage **76.9%** → CRAP 13.8.

This cannot be fixed by tests alone: `CRAP = comp²·(1−cov)³ + comp`, so at complexity 12 even **100% coverage** yields CRAP 12 > 8. The function must be simplified (target complexity ≤ 7, then ≥ ~73% coverage passes; ≤ 6 needs ≥ ~62%). Suggested shape — split the owner resolution out and share it (see the duplication note on `_prListHeadRepo`):

```javascript
function _ghRepoOwnerLogin(repo) {
    var o = repo && repo.owner;
    if (!o) return '';
    return o.login || o.name || '';
}

function _ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr) {
    var r = pr && pr.head && pr.head.repo;
    if (!r) return null;
    if (typeof r === 'string') return r.indexOf('/') !== -1 ? r : null;
    if (r.full_name) return r.full_name;
    if (r.nameWithOwner) return r.nameWithOwner;
    var owner = _ghRepoOwnerLogin(r);
    return owner && r.name ? owner + '/' + r.name : null;
}
```

Also add branch-covering tests for the paths nothing exercises today (`typeof r === 'string'` valid/invalid, `nameWithOwner`) — they are the 23% of uncovered branches here.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

Same gate failure as `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` (see the CI `crap` job, exit code 2). Locally reproduced with the pinned tool and the released baseline: cyclomatic complexity **11**, coverage **54.5%** → CRAP 22.4. At complexity 11 even 100% coverage gives CRAP 11 > 8, so this must be **simplified**, not just tested.

The uncovered branches are exactly the ones the new tests never pass: a string `head.repo`, a repo without `full_name`, and the `owner + name` spelling. Options:

- Extract the small owner-resolution helper (as suggested on `_ghPrHeadRepoFull`) to bring complexity to ≤ 7, and add tests for the string / owner+name shapes.
- Better: this function and `smProvider.js::_ghPrHeadRepoFull` are byte-for-byte the same logic minus the `nameWithOwner` leg — extract **one** resolver, export it from `smProvider.js`, and require it here (`githubSource.js` already requires `../../common/smProvider.js` at line 28). That fixes the gate failure and the duplication in one move.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: near-duplicate head-repo resolvers in two files**

`_prListHeadRepo` here and `_ghPrHeadRepoFull` in `js/common/smProvider.js:446` implement the same contract (resolve `pr.head.repo` to an `owner/repo` full name, null on every malformed shape) with only one difference: the smProvider copy also accepts `nameWithOwner`. The two are already drifting — the GraphQL `nameWithOwner` leg exists in only one of them, and the new tests cover different branch subsets of each.

`githubSource.js` already requires `../../common/smProvider.js` (line 28), so the natural fix is a single exported resolver in `smProvider.js` used by both call sites. That halves the surface the CRAP gate measures and keeps the two PR-list / prStatus payload dialects pinned to one implementation.

**dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (2026-10-18):

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_ghBranchExistsRef` sits exactly at CRAP 8.0 — and the redirect widens the silent-bench case**

Any future branch added here without full coverage immediately breaches the threshold again. Keeping the redirect logic this compact (or folding the owner-parse into the shared resolver from the other comments) leaves headroom.
2. Fail-open semantics note: when the redirect targets a fork the token **cannot read** (private fork the machine has no access to), `branchHead` treats the probe error as "absent" → `branchExists` returns false → a parked fork PR is benched (dropped) rather than kept. That matches pre-PR behavior for forks, so it is not a regression, but it is narrower than the PR description's "throwing probe keeps the item" claim — that only holds when the provider throws (the githubSource `catch`), which `branchExists` never does. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1059
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1059
- **Title**: gh-1057 Dead-head park is fork-blind: branchExists probes the base repo, so restored fork PRs stay parked forever (live: fa #1591)
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1057` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +347
- **Deletions**: -17
- **Created**: 2026-10-18T18:38:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T19:33:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #1057
### Root Cause

The gh-922 dead-head park oracle was fork-blind: `smProvider.js` `branchExists(name)` always probed the deployment's base `owner/repo`, and `githubSource.js` `isDeadHeadParked` passed only the bare branch name — a fork PR's `head.repo` was never consulted. For cross-repo PRs the base-repo probe is a guaranteed 404, so a restored fork branch stayed benched every tick (live: fa PR #1591).

### Fix

- `js/common/smProvider.js`
  - `_ghPrHeadRepoFull(pr)` resolves `pr.head.repo` (`full_name` / owner+name) → `prStatus` now carries `headRepo`.
  - `_ghBranchExistsRef(owner, repo, name, headFull)` redirects the same branchHeads-snapshot + #639 single-branch probe machinery at the head repo when `headFull` names a repo other than the base; absent / same-repo / malformed specs keep the base probe (fail-safe).
  - `branchExists(name, headFull?)` — optional second arg, single-arg callers unchanged.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`
  - `_prItemFromPr` sets `item.headRepo` from the open-PR list payload.
  - `isDeadHeadParked` resolves `item.headRepo || item.pr.headRepo` and passes it to the oracle; all fail-open shapes preserved (no oracle, throwing probe, empty branch → item kept).

### Test Coverage

- RED first: 3 new reproduction tests failed exactly on the bug, then passed after the fix.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smProvider.js` — fork probe redirect (fork snapshot answers, fork 404 benches, no-spec/same-repo/malformed keep base probe); `prStatus.headRepo` for `full_name`, owner+name, and missing-repo shapes.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` — cross-repo PR missing-in-base-but-present-in-fork is NOT benched; gone-from-both stays benched; throwing fork probe keeps the item (fail-open).
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 4318 passed, 0 failed (same-repo regression covered by the pre-existing gh-922 bench tests).

### Notes

- A deleted fork (`head.repo: null`) resolves to `headRepo: null` → base probe → fail-open, same as before.
- Probing a fork costs one `github_list_branches` call per fork repo per tick (separate ioCache namespace), falling back to the existing single-branch `gh api` probe — no new tool surface.
- Rework-on-fork push permissions remain out of scope per the ticket non-goals.
